title: How to Rank in Google AI Overviews (2026 Guide)
excerpt: How to rank in Google AI Overviews: how sources are picked, 9 steps to get cited, AI Overviews vs AI Mode, and how to track AI Overviews honestly.
keywords: how to rank in Google AI Overviews
how to appear in Google AI Overviews
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
To rank in Google AI Overviews, your page has to be indexed and eligible to show a snippet in Google Search. [Google says](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) there are no extra technical requirements and no special markup for AI Overviews or AI Mode. After that, you improve your odds by answering questions directly, covering the related sub-questions Google's AI looks up, showing real expertise, and keeping pages fast, crawlable and current. Nothing guarantees inclusion, so you also need a way to track whether you actually appear.

## How Google AI Overviews work

AI Overviews are the AI-generated summaries that show up at the top of some Google results pages, with links to the pages they drew from. AI Mode is a separate, more conversational search experience where the whole results page is an AI answer and you can ask follow-up questions.

A few points from Google's own documentation (["AI features and your website"](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) on Google Search Central) explain how they behave:

- **They don't appear for every query.** Google shows an AI Overview only when [it decides one adds value](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) beyond classic results. Plenty of searches never trigger one.
- **They use query fan-out.** AI Overviews and AI Mode [may run several related searches](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) across subtopics and data sources to build one response. So the pages linked in an AI Overview aren't always the pages ranking in the top ten for the exact query you typed.
- **They are built on Google's index.** The sources come from pages Google has crawled and [indexed](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features). There's no separate "AI index" you submit to.
- **AI Overviews and AI Mode can differ.** Google notes the two [may use different models and techniques](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), so the links each one shows can vary for the same question.

In short: Google retrieves pages from its index (often through several related searches), its AI models write a summary, and links to supporting pages are shown with the response.

## How Google picks sources for AI Overviews

Google doesn't publish a list of AI Overview ranking factors. [Its guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) is clear on one point, though: the same fundamentals that make a page do well in Search apply here. In practice, a page becomes a likely source when it:

1. **Is eligible.** Indexed, allowed to show a snippet, and meeting [Google's Search technical requirements](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features). A page with `nosnippet` or a very low `max-snippet` value [limits what Google can show](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet) from it.
2. **Matches one of the fan-out queries.** Because Google [may search for subtopics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), a page that answers a narrow sub-question well can be cited even if it doesn't rank for the head term.
3. **Has a passage that can be quoted cleanly.** A clear definition, a short list of steps, or a specific fact stated in context is easier to link to than an idea spread over five paragraphs.
4. **Looks trustworthy.** Google's [helpful, people-first content guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) and E-E-A-T (experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trust) still frame what it wants to surface.
5. **Adds something.** Google's [May 2025 Search Central post on succeeding in AI search](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/05/succeeding-in-ai-search) stresses unique, non-commodity content. If your page repeats what every other result says, there's little reason to cite yours.

## How to rank in Google AI Overviews: step by step

Work through these in order. The first steps are prerequisites. The later ones are where you get ahead of competitors.

### 1. Confirm indexing and snippet eligibility

Open Google Search Console and use the URL Inspection tool on your key pages. Check that:

- The page is indexed and the canonical Google picked is the one you want.
- `robots.txt`, your CDN and your firewall all let Googlebot in.
- You aren't using `nosnippet`, `data-nosnippet` or a restrictive `max-snippet` on content you want quoted.
- The important text is in the HTML Googlebot renders, not hidden behind tabs that only load on click.

A note on `Google-Extended`: [Google's crawler documentation](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers) says it controls whether content Google crawls can be used to train Gemini models and for grounding in the Gemini app and Vertex AI. It is not the control for AI Overviews: [Google's AI features guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) says robots.txt rules for Googlebot are the control for Search, including its AI features. To limit what appears in Search's AI features, use the [preview controls](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet) above (`nosnippet`, `data-nosnippet`, `max-snippet`, `noindex`). Search Console also has a site-wide [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024) (rolled out to all sites in August 2026) that excludes your links and content from AI Overviews and AI Mode. Check it hasn't been switched to "exclude" by mistake.

### 2. Write answer-first passages

Put the direct answer in the first one to three sentences of the page and of each section, then add detail. Use headings phrased the way people search:

```
What is [term]?
How does [process] work?
How much does [service] cost in [city]?
[Option A] vs [Option B]: which is better for [use case]?
How long does [task] take?
```

Under each heading, write a passage that makes sense on its own. If someone copied only that paragraph into an answer, would it still be accurate and complete? That self-contained quality is what makes a passage easy to cite.

### 3. Cover the query fan-out

Since Google expands one question into several related searches, broad topic coverage matters more than ever. For each core topic:

1. Write down the main question.
2. List the follow-ups a real person would ask next (cost, time, risks, alternatives, "for beginners", "for small businesses").
3. Check Google's People Also Ask boxes and related searches for the topic. They're a free view of the sub-questions Google connects to it.
4. Answer each sub-question either in a clear section on the main page or in its own page, linked internally.

This is the same idea behind [answer engine optimization](/answer-engine-optimization): own the specific questions, not just the head keyword.

### 4. Strengthen E-E-A-T signals

Make it obvious who wrote the content and why they're qualified:

- Real author names, short bios, and links to author pages
- First-hand details: photos you took, results you measured, processes you actually run
- Clear sourcing for facts and figures
- An About page, contact details and policies that show a real organization stands behind the site

### 5. Add structured data where it's relevant

[Google says](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) you don't need special schema to appear in AI features. Structured data still helps Google understand your pages, and it supports other rich results. The rule from Google's guidance: markup must match what's visible on the page. Useful types include `Article` (with author and dates), `Product`, `LocalBusiness`, `Organization`, `Recipe` and `Event`, depending on what the page is. Don't add markup for content that isn't there.

### 6. Keep content fresh

For topics that change (pricing, software features, regulations, "best of" lists), outdated pages are, in our view, weaker candidates. Update facts when they change, show a visible "last updated" date, and keep the date honest. Don't change timestamps without changing the content.

### 7. Get page experience right

[Google's AI features guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) specifically mentions page experience, because visitors arriving from an AI Overview should land on a page that works. Make sure pages load quickly, display well on mobile, and keep the main content clearly separate from ads and pop-ups. If someone clicks a citation and gets an interstitial, they leave.

### 8. Support text with images and video

[Google's guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) recommends high-quality images and videos that support your text. Keep the important information in text, but add original diagrams, screenshots, product photos or short how-to videos with descriptive alt text and captions. For local and shopping queries, keep your Google Business Profile and Merchant Center data current; the same guidance lists this too.

### 9. Build authority beyond your own site

In our view, links and mentions from reputable sites still matter, as they do for classic rankings, and they help make your brand a recognizable entity across every AI platform. Our guide to [AI search engine optimization](/blog/ai-search-engine-optimization) covers off-site tactics in more depth.

### What not to do

You may see advice on how to "trick" the AI Overview. Don't. Hidden text, keyword stuffing and mass-produced pages break [Google's spam policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) and hurt the regular rankings AI Overviews depend on.

## AI Overviews vs AI Mode vs featured snippets

These three are easy to confuse. Here's how they compare:

| | AI Overviews | AI Mode | Featured snippets |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What it is** | AI-generated summary at the top of some regular results pages | A separate, conversational AI search experience | A [quoted excerpt](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/featured-snippets) from one page above the organic results |
| **When it shows** | Only when [Google decides it adds value](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) | When the user opens AI Mode | For queries where one passage answers the question well |
| **Sources** | Several linked pages, often found through [fan-out searches](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) | Linked pages, often found through fan-out searches, plus follow-up questions | Usually one page |
| **How content is used** | Summarized and rewritten by AI | Summarized across a multi-turn conversation | Quoted mostly word for word |
| **Eligibility** | [Indexed + snippet-eligible](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) | Indexed + snippet-eligible | Indexed + snippet-eligible |
| **Special markup needed** | [No](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) | No | No |
| **Opt-out controls** | [Preview controls](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet) (`nosnippet`, `data-nosnippet`, `max-snippet`, `noindex`), plus Search Console's [site-wide generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024) | Same as AI Overviews | `nosnippet`, `data-nosnippet`, `max-snippet`, `noindex` |
| **Search Console reporting** | Web search type, plus impressions in the [generative AI performance report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139) | Same as AI Overviews | Web search type |

The takeaway: one solid SEO and content program covers all three. Pages that already win featured snippets often have the answer-first structure AI Overviews favor, but AI Overviews and AI Mode cast a wider net because of fan-out. For how this fits the broader shift, see [GEO vs SEO vs AEO](/blog/geo-vs-seo-vs-aeo).

## How to track Google AI Overviews

This is the hardest part: in our experience, AI Overviews appear inconsistently, vary by location and device, and change from day to day.

### What Google Search Console can and can't tell you

Traffic from AI features (AI Overviews and AI Mode) is [included in your overall Search traffic](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), in the Performance report under the "Web" search type. Google also offers a dedicated [generative AI performance report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139) in Search Console, rolled out to all sites on August 31, 2026.

That means:

- You **can** see how many impressions your site gets in Search's generative AI features, broken down by page, country, device and date ([Google's report documentation](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139)).
- You **can't** see clicks, click-through rate or queries in that report. [Google's documentation](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139) lists impressions only, and says it expects to update the report's coverage over time.
- You **can't** split the report into AI Overviews versus AI Mode. Both are counted together as [generative AI features](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139).
- A drop in click-through rate on a query that holds its position can still hint that an AI Overview appeared, but you'll need a manual check or a tracker to confirm it for a specific query.

So Search Console now tells you which pages appear in Google's AI features, but not which queries trigger them or how many clicks they send. Check Google's current Search Console documentation, since reporting is still changing.

### Manual AI Overview checks

For a small keyword set, manual checks work:

1. Open a private/incognito window and sign out of Google to reduce personalization.
2. Set the location that matters to you. Results differ by country and city, so use Google's location settings or a VPN where appropriate.
3. Search each target query on desktop and on mobile.
4. Note whether an AI Overview appears, and click to expand it if it's collapsed.
5. Repeat on a regular schedule (weekly for priority terms), because one check is a snapshot, not a verdict.

### Dedicated AI Overview trackers

To check more than a few dozen keywords, use a tool. Some rank trackers and SEO platforms now detect AI Overviews in the results pages they monitor, including these two:

- **SE Ranking** has an [AI Overviews tracker](https://seranking.com/ai-overviews-tracker.html) that records whether keywords trigger an AI Overview, where your site appears in it, which other sources are cited, and cached copies of those results pages. It also has a separate AI Mode tracker.
- **Seobility** has an [AI Overview tracker](https://www.seobility.net/en/ai-overview-tracker/) built into its ranking monitoring. According to Seobility's site (October 2026), the free plan only shows whether an AI Overview appears for tracked keywords. Premium plans add the full answer text, all cited sources and their order, whether your site is cited, and daily updates.

Others in this category include standalone AI Overview checkers and AI visibility suites. Compare them on locations covered, update frequency, mobile vs desktop, and whether they store the full answer text. Features change often, so check each vendor's current documentation.

### Checklist: what to record for each query

Whether you track manually or with a tool, log the same fields every time:

- Query, date, location, device
- AI Overview shown? (yes/no)
- Your domain cited? Which URL?
- Your brand mentioned in the answer text, and how it's described
- Other domains cited (especially competitors)
- Your classic organic position for the same query
- Whether a featured snippet or other SERP features appeared
- For AI Mode: same fields, tracked separately

### The bigger picture beyond Google

AI Overviews are one AI surface among several. Your buyers may also be asking ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and the Gemini app. AI Brand Track doesn't track Google AI Overviews or AI Mode. It covers those four assistants: you enter your website, and it queries ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini with prompts for your industry, then reports a 0-100 visibility score, competitor rankings, sentiment and share of voice in about a minute. Pairing an AI Overview tracker with a cross-platform view gives you the full [AI search visibility](/ai-search-visibility) picture. For the manual and automated methods, see [how to track brand visibility in AI platforms](/blog/how-to-track-brand-visibility-in-ai-platforms).

## What to do if you lose traffic to AI Overviews

If clicks fall on queries where you still rank, AI Overviews may be answering the question before users scroll. Some practical responses:

1. **Diagnose first.** In Search Console, compare impressions, clicks and CTR by query before and after the drop, and check the generative AI performance report to see which pages are getting AI feature impressions. Then manually check whether those queries now show an AI Overview. Rule out other causes too: core updates, technical issues, seasonality.
2. **Check whether you're cited.** If an AI Overview appears and you're not linked, review which pages are cited and what they cover that you don't.
3. **Shift toward content that earns the click.** Simple factual answers are easy to summarize. Original data, tools, calculators, detailed comparisons, templates and first-hand reviews give people a reason to visit.
4. **Target follow-up and decision-stage queries.** Fan-out means more sub-questions get answered. Make sure you own the deeper, commercial ones ("X vs Y for small teams", "X pricing", "X alternatives").
5. **Measure value, not just volume.** Visitors who click through from an AI result may be further along in their decision. Track conversions per landing page, not only sessions.
6. **Diversify.** Build email lists, communities and presence on the other AI platforms where your audience researches, rather than relying on one traffic source.

The broader framework for this is [generative engine optimization](/generative-engine-optimization): optimizing to be cited and recommended in AI-generated answers wherever they appear.

## FAQ

### How do I get ranked in an AI Overview?

Make sure your page is indexed and eligible to show a snippet, which is the only technical requirement [Google lists](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features). Then write answer-first passages under question-style headings, cover the related sub-questions people ask, and show clear expertise and sourcing. Google doesn't guarantee inclusion, so track your target queries over time.

### What triggers Google AI Overviews?

[Google shows an AI Overview](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) when its systems decide an AI summary adds value beyond the regular results. In our experience, that tends to happen for informational and multi-part questions more than for simple navigational searches. Whether one appears can vary by query wording, location, device and day.

### How do I track AI Overviews?

Combine manual checks (incognito, signed out, correct location, desktop and mobile) with a dedicated tracker if you monitor many keywords. Rank trackers and SEO platforms such as [SE Ranking](https://seranking.com/ai-overviews-tracker.html) and [Seobility](https://www.seobility.net/en/ai-overview-tracker/) now record when AI Overviews appear and which sites they cite. Log the same fields each time, including whether you're cited and which competitors are.

### Can I track clicks from AI Overviews in Google Search Console?

Not clicks, but you can now see impressions. Search Console's [generative AI performance report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139) shows how often your pages appeared in AI Overviews and AI Mode (combined), by page, country, device and date. It doesn't show clicks, CTR or queries, and AI feature clicks stay mixed into the regular Performance report under the [Web search type](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features). To see which queries trigger an AI Overview and whether you're cited, you still need manual checks or a third-party tracker.

### Do I need special schema or an llms.txt file to appear in AI Overviews?

No. [Google says](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) there are no additional requirements, no special schema.org markup and no AI-specific text files needed for AI Overviews or AI Mode. Structured data can still help Google understand your page and support other rich results, as long as it matches the visible content.

### Can Google rank AI-generated content?

Yes, if it's helpful. [Google's guidance on AI-generated content](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/02/google-search-and-ai-content) focuses on content quality, not how it was produced. Using automation mainly to manipulate rankings violates its [spam policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies), though. Unedited, generic AI text rarely adds the unique value that makes a page worth citing in an AI Overview.

### Why am I not getting an AI Overview?

As a searcher, you may not see one because Google only shows AI Overviews when [its systems decide they add something](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) beyond classic results, so many queries never trigger one. As a site owner, if your pages aren't cited, check indexing, snippet controls and your Search Console generative AI control first, then compare your content against the pages that are cited.

### Is AI Overview like ChatGPT?

Both use large language models to write answers, but they work differently. AI Overviews sit inside Google Search, draw on Google's index, and [appear only for some queries](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features). ChatGPT is a standalone assistant that answers from its [training data](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) or from its own [web search](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt). Being visible in one doesn't guarantee visibility in the other, so it's worth checking both. You can [run a free AI visibility check](/register) for ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini.
